result: In Fukuda CFS without major depression (51 vs 20 controls), psychomotor/processing speed was slower (TMT-A p=0.027, digit-symbol substitution p=0.004, copy p=0.007, scanning p=0.034) while most measures were in the average range; Stroop differences reflected processing speed, not inhibition.
reason: Independent cohort shows processing-speed deficit, same direction, not explained by depression.

result: Within CFS, lower HRV correlated with slower processing (digit-symbol copy r=0.33, substitution r=0.31, Stroop colour naming r=0.28); no case-control HRV difference is reported in the abstract.
reason: Does not test HRV versus controls; adds a correlation of HRV with cognitive slowing, so extends rather than replicates.

result: In 22 ME/CFS vs 22 sedentary controls, exercise-induced change in pressure pain threshold correlated with change in C4a (thumb r=0.67 after submaximal exercise; calf r=0.43 after self-paced; R2=0.24) only in patients; elastase was unrelated.
reason: Secondary analysis of exercise-hyperalgesia data proposing a complement mechanism; small and only 1 of 3 PPT sites associated.

result: Post-exercise C4a changes in ME/CFS (n=22) correlated with changes in pain thresholds (r=0.67 and 0.43), not seen in controls; elastase activity changes were not associated.
reason: Links the exercise C4a response to post-exertional pain sensitisation; does not itself report C4a levels vs controls.

result: Systematic review of 7 small studies: microbiome differences reported in all, only 3 significant, inconsistent across studies, poor quality; insufficient evidence that dysbiosis plays a role in CFS/ME.
reason: Abstract gives no specific taxon-severity associations; too thin to test the severity-link claim, and predates the cohorts the finding rests on.

result: Systematic review of 7 small studies: microbiome differences reported in all, only 3 significant, inconsistent findings, poor quality; insufficient evidence for dysbiosis.
reason: Does not examine butyrate producers or butyrate capacity specifically; a general pre-2018 review of poor-quality studies.

result: Meta-analysis of 32 studies: peak VO2 5.2 (95% CI 3.8-6.6) ml/kg/min lower in CFS/ME than healthy controls, tau 3.4, prediction interval -1.9 to 12.2.
reason: already cited (this is the Teesside Franklin meta-analysis listed as 'Franklin 2018/2021'; the 5 ml/kg/min figure in the claim comes from it).

result: Meta-analysis of 32 studies: peak VO2 5.2 ml/kg/min lower in CFS/ME than apparently healthy controls, with substantial heterogeneity.
reason: Compares with healthy controls only; does not address whether deconditioning explains the deficit. Only fitting finding (low peak VO2) already cites it.

result: In the UK ME/CFS Biobank (272 ME/CFS, 136 healthy, 76 MS, 37 other chronic fatigue), hand grip strength across 3 repeats was reduced in ME/CFS, most in severe patients (minimum HGS 15.3 kg lower than healthy controls, 95% CI 11.3-19.3), and tracked severity measures.
reason: Independent multi-centre cohort with disease comparators; same measure, lower strength linked to severity.

result: Of 627 ME/CFS adults on 10-min tilt, 155 (25%) met POTS criteria; median time to HR criterion was 3 min, so a 2-min tilt would miss 55% (95% CI 48-63%) of POTS cases, regardless of sex, age, duration or hypocapnia.
reason: Main result is that POTS prevalence depends on tilt protocol duration, which is the neuro-pots-prevalence claim; it does not test cerebral hypoperfusion or preload.
